who: People working in a second language
takeaways: Context-sensitive help is available: help about the specific field or task where people are, not just a general help center.
Level AAA. It goes further than 3.3.2 (A), which asks for labels or instructions where input is needed. This adds help at the point of need.
It can be hint text below a field, a worked example, a “What is this?” link next to a tricky field, or a short guide at the start of a complex form.
Help is most needed where the label alone is not enough: tax numbers, policy choices, technical settings.
failures: A tricky field with only a label
Help that lives only in a separate FAQ
Hint text that disappears once people start typing
check: Walk the form as a first-time user. Mark every field where you would need to ask someone.
For each mark, point to the help on the same screen.
Check the help can be reached by keyboard and touch, not only by hover.

quiz.question: An insurance form asks people to choose an excess amount. The label says “Excess”. What best meets 3.3.5?
options: A link to the general help center in the footer
A tooltip that appears only on hover over the label
A short line below the field explaining what excess means, with an example
quiz.why: Help that sits with the field and is always visible is context-sensitive and reachable by everyone. A help center link is general, and hover tooltips leave out keyboard and touch users.

spec: Write hint text for every field that needs it, and mark which fields have “More info” links.
Design the help pattern: inline hint, disclosure or side panel, and say how it opens.
Link each help item to its field, so it can be read with the field.
review: Where would a first-time user get stuck here?
Can I get help without leaving the page?
Is this help written for experts or for the people filling it in?
tradeoff: Help text everywhere makes forms long and noisy. Fully meeting this AAA rule rarely means help on every field: add it where research or support tickets show people get stuck, and keep it short.
system: Give the field component optional hint and “More info” slots, so help can be added without a custom design.
pitch: Every question people cannot answer on the page becomes a support call or an abandoned form. Help in place is cheaper.
